correctness.rationale: The exact support function is the sum of the q largest coordinates minus the sum of the q smallest. Sorting partitions the weighted-mean-zero hyperplane into simplicial step-ray cones, where width is linear. Positive definiteness and strict triangle inequality prove that only single step rays can achieve minimum width. Each ray has explicit squared weighted norm A_SB_S/T and top-minus-bottom range min(|S|,n-|S|,q), producing the complete weighted theorem and normalized normals. For unit scales, monotonicity leaves only singleton and balanced splits, and the factored sign test gives the threshold n=4q²-1. Rational finite checks reproduced 566297 tested profiles and transition equalities. No finite experiment is used as a universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact arbitrary-rank minimum Euclidean width, all minimizing directions, and the sharp integer transition at dimension equal to four times the squared smaller rank minus one were not found in the checked hypersimplex or regular-simplex primary material. The 2023 regular-simplex result is a covered q=1 case and is not claimed. Projection-skeleton classifications and matroid valuations cannot imply the metric width and its minimizing unit normals without new Euclidean optimization. The weighted subset theorem includes every positive diagonal scaling. Priority is provisional, especially against older sources indexed as thickness or order-statistic norm.

value.rationale: The canonical hypersimplex (uniform-matroid base polytope) is a natural infinite family of rank-selected cube slices. Its least Euclidean thickness is a structural invariant and its minimizing normal supports encode geometry of its extreme projections. A sharp quadratic change from only coordinate directions to exponentially many balanced directions is a mathematically motivated complete classification; the positive-diagonal formula supplies a robust structural generalization useful for anisotropic realizations. The finding is not a small numerical improvement or a renamed simplex result.
